analysis.title: Earnings & Central Bank Decisions / German Business Sentiment / Oil Retreats
key_insights: This week is dominated by corporate earnings and central bank meetings. In the US, 44.5% of S&P and 38% of Nasdaq market cap reports. Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon need to show that cloud revenue, cash generation and infrastructure returns can keep pace with accelerating capex after the AI selloff.

UBS says a generic demand beat is no longer enough. Investors want proof that revenue arrives before financing costs and depreciation overwhelm the return. The AI financing premium can fade if hyperscaler results deliver, given the substantial de-grossing and systematic selling.

The Fed, BoC, RBNZ, ECB and BoJ all meet within a 72-hour window and the expected theme is hawkishness. UBS's Pingle expects the FOMC to hold on Wednesday with a hawkish tilt. The BoJ and ECB are also expected to pause with hawkish signals. UBS expects the BoC to hike 25bp to 2.50% and the RBNZ to hike 25bp to 3.00%. Dissents are likely to favor doing more.

German ifo rose 0.3 points to 90.2 in October (consensus 90), the highest since May 2023. Expectations rose 1.2 points to 91.6 (consensus 90). Current conditions fell 0.7 points to 88.8 (consensus 89.9). UBS expects Q3 GDP of 0.1% q/q and Q4 of 0.3% q/q.

Brent is at $115.08/bbl and WTI at $101.24/bbl, down about 1.8-2.2% from Friday. Brent settled Friday at $116.72, a six-month high. The rally came from escalating US-Iran tensions, and diplomatic signals are now trimming some of the risk premium. Crude in floating storage rose 8% w/w to 87.42 million barrels as of October 23 (Vortexa).

Lula was re-elected with 51.76% to Flavio Bolsonaro's 48.24%. The desk expects a significant repricing of Brazilian assets on Monday, with USDBRL potentially at 5.3. The EM strategist sees USDBRL at 5.5-5.6 by end-2026, a 100-150bp rise in rates, and a 10-15% equity correction based on the latest EWZ reaction.
Moody's left France at Aa3 (negative outlook). OATs were indicated about 5.5bp tighter and EU bonds 0.5-1bp tighter. Moody's said the rating assumes a deficit-reducing 2027 budget is adopted.
RBA chief economist Hunter said rates may need to rise again with the cash rate at a 15-year high of 4.6%. UBS Economics sees another 25bp hike, most likely in November.

Japanese life insurers are focused on JGBs rather than foreign bonds. Year-end 10y JGB expectations are 3.0%-3.3% (some up to 3.6%), 30y 4.0%-4.4%, and USDJPY 155-158. Foreign bond interest is selective, in US investment-grade and private credit.

UK long-end flattening looks crowded and near fair value. The desk prefers long-end steepeners and shorter-dated flatteners, or 2s5s30s structures. The UK budget on Wednesday will outline a path to 3.5% of GDP on core defence by 2035.

Nearly 25% of S&P market cap has reported Q3. 78% are beating, revenues are growing 12.5% and earnings are tracking 31% higher y/y. Hedge funds are selling AI winners and momentum. Long exposure has fallen from the 90th to the 15th percentile since September, while shorts rose from the 15th to the 80th. Equity long/short strategies are down 7% in October and quant funds are flat.

UBS derivatives strategy says the medium-term bullish US equity view remains intact. Long-duration capital drives the destination and short-duration systematic and hedge fund capital drives the path, so deleveraging is more likely to create temporary dislocations than a durable reversal.

UBS equity strategy sees AI credit stress as concentrated, not broad. Hyperscaler spreads are broadly stable, with yields up mainly on Treasury yields except at Oracle. Neoclouds are 5-7% of expected AI datacentre capex. Six hyperscalers are forecast to invest $7.7 trn over 2026-30, and a 15% ROIC by 2031 needs $1 trn of incremental EBIT and about $3.4 trn of revenue.

KOSPI 12m forward P/E is 4.2x. SK Hynix plans a special dividend of about KRW16 trn (~USD12 bn). SK Hynix reports Wednesday and Samsung Thursday. The desk has a sell skew across quant, long-only and ETF flows, and is better to sell Japan, Hong Kong and Korea.
European AI winners fell over 8% while defensives gained. Desk flows sold semis and hardware and bought healthcare. Banks closed below major support.

FX trading sees gold support at 3,970-3,975 and 3,945-3,950 with resistance at 4,025-4,035. It prefers re-entering silver shorts at 54.30-54.50, invalidated above 55.10-55.20. USDJPY has 50-day moving average resistance near 157.50-157.55, and USDCAD resistance is at 1.4040-1.4050.

sector_views.rationale: Hyperscaler earnings must show returns keep pace with capex. The desk is a net seller of Technology and Financials in Asia flows.
European defensives gained and healthcare was bought on strong results while AI winners fell over 8%.

risk_factors: Hawkish central bank surprises across the Fed, ECB, BoJ, BoC and RBNZ.
Second-round effects from higher energy prices in Europe.
US-Iran escalation and elevated oil supply risk.
Brazil fiscal trajectory and a repricing of Brazilian assets.
French fiscal and political risk, with possible spillover to Italian BTP spreads.
Hyperscaler returns failing to cover financing costs and depreciation, and concentrated credit stress at leveraged AI issuers.
Labor-market weakness, prolonged inflation, geopolitical shocks or fading US exceptionalism could erode the US equity trend.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund long exposure fell from the 90th to the 15th percentile since September, shorts rose from the 15th to the 80th, and nets are in the 25th percentile.
Equity long/short strategies are down 7% in October and quant funds are flat (UBS Knowledge Network).
The derisking is comparable in size to July. The flow picture has been supportive despite the unwind.
The desk starts the week with a sell skew across quant funds, long-only investors and ETFs in Asia.
UK long-end flattening looks crowded and stretched.
In Europe, banks closed below major support, with stocks sold but baskets and indices bought.
geopolitical: Escalating US-Iran tensions. Trump said it is "getting to be decision time" on a deal with Tehran or to "finish it off." Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials are traveling to Iran for regional security talks.
Lula won a fourth term in Brazil. Flavio Bolsonaro sought an annulment of the runoff and alleged voter suppression.
France: renewed weekend protests passed without serious incidents, and Moody's held the Aa3 rating with a negative outlook.
UK to set out a path to a NATO defence target of 3.5% of GDP on core defence by 2035 in Wednesday's budget.
